answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens per gem color and 5 gold; reveal 3 nobles. Remove unrevealed nobles permanently.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 players = 4 gems/color, 5 gold, 3 nobles. Noble Tile Mechanics: removed nobles are out permanently.

answers.answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles; two more gems per color, one more noble, same gold.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level deck separately. Arrange level 1 at bottom, level 2 in middle, level 3 on top. Reveal 4 cards per level (12 total). The youngest player starts and play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player.

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 3 different non-gold gems; take 2 same-color non-gold gems if at least 4 are in supply; reserve one card if holding fewer than 3 reserved and take gold if available; or purchase one face-up or previously reserved card. You cannot take gems then buy, or reserve then buy that card in the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one" action; purchase reserved on "a previous turn."

answers.answer: All owned tokens must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: Yes, take two green from four, leaving two. No, cannot take two red from three. Check before taking. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them"; gem actions specify "no gold."

answers.answer: Temporarily holding twelve is allowed. Return two tokens of your choice, including newly drawn gems if desired. Gold counts toward the ten-token limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: may temporarily exceed 10; may return "some or all of the tokens they just took"; limit includes gold.

answers.answer: Take the gold, reaching eleven temporarily; return one token, possibly that gold, to finish at ten. If gold is empty, reserve with no gold and remain at ten.
answers.evidence: Reserve: empty gold does not prevent reservation. Token Hand Limit permits returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card of any level deck. Take a deck-top card without showing opponents. Only its reserving player may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: top card "without revealing it"; reserved cards purchased only by reserving player.

answers.answer: No reservation with three already reserved, even just for gold. Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room: purchasing it is the only way it leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; only removal is purchase.

answers.answer: Immediately refill from the top of the level-2 deck. The same applies to buying a face-up card. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy to refill. If the relevant deck is empty, the vacant space stays empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: face-up purchases and reservations are immediately replaced from the same level; empty deck leaves space empty.

answers.answer: Spend one green token, no blue. If bonuses cover the full cost, spend no tokens. Bonuses remain permanently and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact 2-blue/1-green example; sufficient bonuses allow no-token purchases; bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Yes. After bonuses, pay one blue token for the remaining blue and two gold for the remaining black and white. All spent tokens return to supply; bonus cards stay with you.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce costs, gold substitutes for any gem, spent gems and gold return to supply; bonuses permanent.

answers.answer: Buy one face-up market card or one previously reserved card. Arrange purchased cards face up before you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so bonuses and prestige values are visible to all at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card, including final arrangement paragraph.

answers.answer: No: a white or gold token cannot replace the missing white bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn. Excess bonuses are allowed.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: requires "at least" the bonuses; "bonuses only ... not gem tokens"; checked at end of turn.

answers.answer: Choose one; cannot take both or refuse all visits. The other remains available. This costs no action, gives 3 prestige, and is checked at the end of your turn after your action.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: automatic, not an action, choose one, maximum one per turn, 3 points.

answers.answer: Put the received noble face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you."

answers.answer: C and D still play; A does not play again. B is not guaranteed to win: another player may surpass B during the final round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger completes current round for equal turns; End-of-Game Clarifications says trigger player may be surpassed.

answers.answer: Your total is 16. Yes, 15 or more triggers the end condition. Determine the winner after the current round finishes with equal turn counts.
answers.evidence: Nobles worth 3; End-Game Trigger: "15 or more"; winner has most points at end of final round.

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie at 16, then B wins with 9 purchased developments versus 10. C has fewer prestige, so card count does not help. Noble points count. B’s three reserved cards are unpurchased and do not count in the purchased-card tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: most prestige, including nobles. Tiebreaker: fewest development cards purchased.

answers.answer: No printed points or bonuses on unpurchased reserved cards count toward score, trigger, purchase discounts, or nobles. Those benefits require purchased developments.
answers.evidence: Scoring refers to "each purchased card"; payment bonuses from "previously purchased" cards; nobles use bonuses from purchased cards.

answers.answer: No physical token is received. The zero-point card still supplies a permanent blue discount for future purchases and a bonus for noble requirements.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: purchased cards add one permanent bonus and "never generate tokens"; cards may be worth 0; nobles require bonuses.

answers.answer: Its own bonus cannot make it free: discounts come from previously purchased cards. The newly purchased white bonus does count for the noble at the end of this same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "previously purchased development cards"; turn sequence checks noble eligibility after the action.

answers.answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs or produce blue change. You still need two green tokens, with gold permitted as substitutes for either or both.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess gives no benefit and no change; bonuses are color-specific; gold substitutes for any gem.

answers.answer: Bonuses remain permanently. Taking gems next turn can be followed by receiving the still-available other noble. You cannot collect it on an opponent’s intervening turn: noble checks occur at the end of your own turn.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "At the end of their turn"; other nobles remain available for future turns; bonuses permanent.

answers.answer: Yes, reserve the expensive level-3 card without paying its printed cost, and take gold if available. Reservation has no affordability requirement in the described action.
answers.evidence: Reserve permits any face-up development or deck top, takes it into hand plus gold; payment is specified for purchasing.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled: twelve remain. You take only the one deck-top card into your hand, without a second replacement card.
answers.evidence: Reserve: take "one development card" from deck top; replacement applies to face-up grid acquisitions.

answers.answer: The four face-up cards remain available for purchase or reservation. Purchasing one leaves its space empty because its deck is exhausted; the other three remain available.
answers.evidence: Purchasing/reserving permits face-up cards; Card Replacement: exhausted deck leaves the empty space empty for the rest of the game.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the reserved card or take three different gems. Continue legal actions until the normal prestige end condition.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger explicitly says deck or market exhaustion does not end the game; remaining legal actions include reserved purchases.

answers.answer: Yes. Take three, temporarily reaching thirteen, then return all three new tokens to end with the same ten. No net token gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit permits temporary excess and returning "some or all of the tokens they just took."

answers.answer: A returns both spent gold to supply; B can take one. One gold remains in supply immediately after B’s reservation, before any returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: spent gold returned to supply. Reserving takes one gold if available.

answers.answer: Yes. You may purchase the affordable face-up level-3 card; the purchase action does not require owning lower-level cards first.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card permits a face-up development from the grid by paying its cost, without level prerequisites.

answers.answer: You cannot refuse the automatic noble. You finish with 18 prestige: 12 + 3 for the development + 3 for the noble. Other players with turns left in this round continue.
answers.evidence: Noble visits cannot be refused and give 3 points; End-Game Trigger completes the current round with equal turns.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes the turn. A does not begin another round and nobody gets an extra turn, since all four have equal turn counts at that point.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round so every player has played the same number of turns.

answers.answer: No replacement noble is revealed: removed nobles are permanently out. The acquired noble goes face up before the receiving player; two remain available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: removed tiles out permanently; received noble placed face up before player.

answers.answer: Emerald green, diamond white, sapphire blue, onyx black, ruby red, gold joker yellow. There are 90 developments: 40 level 1, 30 level 2, 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token-color and development-card tables.

answers.answer: You may pay gold and keep green. The gold substitutes for the required green token and returns to the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: gold "can substitute for any single gem token"; spent gold returned to supply.

answers.answer: Yes. The four-token minimum applies to taking two of one color, not three different colors. Taking one from each leaves zero red, one blue, and two green.
answers.evidence: Different-color action takes one each from three piles; only same-color action specifies the four-token threshold.

answers.answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange is not a listed action or the stated use of gold. Gold substitutes for a required gem token when buying a development.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists four actions; Gold Token Specifics allows substitution "when purchasing a card."

answers.answer: You must perform exactly one of the four actions; voluntarily passing with legal actions available is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one of the following four actions."
